views.name: orders_clean_timestamps
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  order_status,
  order_purchase_timestamp,
  order_approved_at,
  order_delivered_carrier_date,
  order_delivered_customer_date,
  order_estimated_delivery_date,
  -- derived flags indicating presence of lifecycle timestamps
  (order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL) AS has_order_purchase_timestamp,
  (order_approved_at IS NOT NULL) AS has_order_approved_at,
  (order_delivered_carrier_date IS NOT NULL) AS has_order_delivered_carrier_date,
  (order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL) AS has_order_delivered_customer_date,
  (order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL) AS has_order_estimated_delivery_date
FROM orders
views.description: Normalize and expose order timestamps as ISO8601-compatible TEXT and boolean flags about key lifecycle events. Useful as a cleaned orders projection for downstream joins, time-based aggregations, and lifecycle calculations. | Use for: time-to-ship / delivery latency per order; counts of orders by lifecycle completion (approved/delivered); filter orders by presence/absence of specific timestamps

views.name: order_items_with_product_and_seller
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.order_id,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.product_id,
  oi.seller_id,
  oi.shipping_limit_date,
  oi.price,
  oi.freight_value,
  p.product_category_name,
  p.product_name_lenght,
  p.product_description_lenght,
  p.product_photos_qty,
  p.product_weight_g,
  p.product_length_cm,
  p.product_height_cm,
  p.product_width_cm,
  s.seller_zip_code_prefix,
  s.seller_city,
  s.seller_state
FROM order_items oi
LEFT JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN sellers s ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id
views.description: Denormalize order_items with product attributes and seller attributes. Useful for queries needing item-level pricing, product dimensions, category, and seller location in the same row. | Use for: order-line level revenue or freight analysis; product category sales by seller location; analyzing item-level dimensions vs shipping limits

views.name: order_payments_aggregated
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_rows_count,
  SUM(payment_value) AS payment_value_sum,
  AVG(payment_value) AS payment_value_avg,
  MIN(payment_installments) AS payment_installments_min,
  MAX(payment_installments) AS payment_installments_max,
  -- most common payment_type per order derived by ordering types by frequency and picking the first via GROUP_CONCAT trick
  (SELECT split.value
   FROM (
     SELECT
       payment_type || '|' || COUNT(*) AS kt,
       payment_type AS value
     FROM order_payments op2
     WHERE op2.order_id = op.order_id
     GROUP BY payment_type
     ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, payment_type ASC
   ) AS split
   LIMIT 1) AS payment_type_mode
FROM order_payments op
GROUP BY order_id
views.description: Aggregate payments per order to produce order-level payment totals, count of payment rows, and dominant payment_type via MAX(payment_type) over counts (useful but not authoritative for ties). Useful when you need a single-row-per-order payment summary. | Use for: reconcile order totals vs payments; payment method distribution and common installment counts; identify orders with split/multiple payments

views.name: customer_order_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.customer_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders_count,
  MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS first_order_purchase_timestamp,
  MAX(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS last_order_purchase_timestamp
FROM orders o
GROUP BY o.customer_id
views.description: Compute per-customer order counts and first/last order timestamps. Useful for segmentation, recency/frequency analysis, and downstream joins to customer attributes. | Use for: RFM / customer recency-frequency analysis; churn or engagement cohorts; join with customers to profile high-frequency buyers

views.name: product_category_translation_lookup
views.description: Simple lookup table mapping original product_category_name to English translation. Useful for queries that need category names in English; safe to left-join from products. | Use for: translate product category names for reporting; group sales by translated category

views.name: geolocation_by_zip_best
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  AVG(geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat,
  AVG(geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng,
  -- most frequent city/state via subqueries
  (SELECT geolocation_city FROM geolocation g2 WHERE g2.geolocation_zip_code_prefix = g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix GROUP BY geolocation_city ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, geolocation_city ASC LIMIT 1) AS geolocation_city,
  (SELECT geolocation_state FROM geolocation g3 WHERE g3.geolocation_zip_code_prefix = g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix GROUP BY geolocation_state ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, geolocation_state ASC LIMIT 1) AS geolocation_state
FROM geolocation g
GROUP BY geolocation_zip_code_prefix
views.description: Collapse geolocation samples to one representative lat/lng per geolocation_zip_code_prefix by taking the average lat/lng and most frequent city/state. Useful when joining geolocation by zip prefix to customers or sellers. | Use for: map customers/sellers to lat/lng by zip prefix; spatial aggregation of orders/sales by zip centroid

views.name: order_reviews_per_order
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  COUNT(review_id) AS reviews_count,
  AVG(review_score) AS review_score_avg,
  MIN(review_creation_date) AS first_review_creation_date,
  MAX(review_creation_date) AS last_review_creation_date
FROM order_reviews
GROUP BY order_id
views.description: Aggregate reviews at the order level: count of reviews, average review_score, and first/last review timestamps. Useful to link order satisfaction signals to order records. | Use for: customer satisfaction per order; correlate reviews with delivery times or sellers

views.name: orders_with_items_payments_reviews
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  oi_agg.items_count,
  oi_agg.items_price_sum,
  oi_agg.items_freight_sum,
  pay.payment_rows_count,
  pay.payment_value_sum,
  rev.reviews_count,
  rev.review_score_avg
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS items_count, SUM(price) AS items_price_sum, SUM(freight_value) AS items_freight_sum
  FROM order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
) oi_agg ON o.order_id = oi_agg.order_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS payment_rows_count, SUM(payment_value) AS payment_value_sum
  FROM order_payments
  GROUP BY order_id
) pay ON o.order_id = pay.order_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(review_id) AS reviews_count, AVG(review_score) AS review_score_avg
  FROM order_reviews
  GROUP BY order_id
) rev ON o.order_id = rev.order_id
views.description: Wide denormalized order-level view joining orders to aggregated payments, aggregated reviews, and item-level aggregates (total price and freight per order). Useful for order-level analytics without duplicating order_items rows. | Use for: order-level revenue and satisfaction analysis; modeling delivered vs paid vs reviewed orders; aggregate KPIs per order for reporting

views.name: customer_ranking_by_recency_frequency
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  co.orders_count,
  co.last_order_purchase_timestamp,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY co.last_order_purchase_timestamp DESC) AS recency_rank,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY co.orders_count DESC) AS frequency_rank
FROM (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders_count, MAX(order_purchase_timestamp) AS last_order_purchase_timestamp
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY customer_id
) co
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = co.customer_id
views.description: Compute per-customer rank by recency (last order) and frequency (orders_count). Exposes recency_rank and frequency_rank to support top-K selection downstream. Useful for customer segmentation and targeting. | Use for: select top customers by recency or frequency; create target lists for retention campaigns; RFM-style segmentation when combined with monetary metrics
